newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel unlinked bonds end up on inflation hopes.
newsitem.headline: Israel unlinked bonds end up on inflation hopes.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher across the board on Thursday, with most of the activity focused on unlinked bonds, which gained on expectations for declining inflation, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.04 pct to 170.43.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.10 pct to 161.09
Volume was high at 224 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds and Makams.

"Wednesday's positive trend continued today with CPI-linked (consumer price index) bonds rising again. The highest rise was posted by long bonds, which rose 0.3 percent, while the short bonds gained only 0.1 percent," said Gidi Halperin at Meitav Securities and Investments.

"Demand for inflation linked-bonds rose again today, but yields on the long bonds remain stable at around 4.5 percent. It seems the market will remain stable at the current level," said Hanna Prisan, head of Bank Hapoalim's securities department.
"Unlinked bonds continue to be very attractive and activity is high. With expectations for annual inflation of eight to 10 percent in 1997 they offer very nice yields," Prisan added.
"Activity in the unlinked bonds continues to be high. Investors predict the Bank of Israel will lower interest rates in the near future, after the government approves the budget cuts," Halperin said.

Traders said unlinked bonds did not post higher gains because mutual funds that specialise in unlinked bonds had to sell bonds before the end of the month to enjoy tax benefits. They said unlinked bonds are expected to rise further on Sunday, the next day of trading in Israel.
"Makams also rose today and they reflect hopes for annual (1997) inflation of 9.5 percent, which is relatively low," Halperin added.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds closed higher following the shekel's decline against the U.S. currency.
On Thursday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2570 shekels against 3.2520 on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
